articleTitle: Land Change Detection in Sentinel-2 Images Using IR-MAD And Deep Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Earth Observation and Geo-Spatial Information (ICEOGI)
abstract: This paper presents a method for land change detection in bi-temporal satellite images using deep neural network (DNN) which is seen as the simplest deep learning (DL) architecture. Unlike the conventional change detection methods, the DL-based approaches do not require a large amount of existing knowledge about the study area. Consequently, no human intervention is necessary during the training step leading to the improvement of the change detection automation process. The proposed method uses a DNN algorithm whose inputs are binary training data (change, no change) and the iteratively reweighted multivariate alteration detection (IR-MAD) components. The IR-MAD channels calculated from the bi-temporal satellite images already contain change information, which might guide the DNN to automatically extract more robust features and then to produce more accurate change detection mapping. The performance of the implemented algorithm is verified by using co-registered bi-temporal multispectral images acquired in 2017 and 2022 by Sentinel-2 satellite over the North Eastern part of Algiers city (Algeria). The obtained results are promising and show that the proposed DNN change detection method is more accurate compared to usual conventional methods in terms of statistical precision (Overall accuracy, Kappa coefficient, spectral signature).

articleTitle: Flood-Prone Urban Area Mapping Using Machine Learning, a Case Study of M'sila City (Algeria)
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Earth Observation and Geo-Spatial Information (ICEOGI)
abstract: This study aims to develop a flood sensitivity assessment tool using machine learning (ML) techniques and geographic information system (GIS). The importance of this study is integrating the geographic information systems (GIS) and machine learning (ML) techniques for mapping flood risks, which help decision-makers to identify the most vulnerable areas and take the necessary precautions to face this type of natural disaster. To reach this goal, we will study the case of the city of M'sila, which is among the areas most vulnerable to floods. This study drew a map of flood-prone areas based on the methodology where we have made a comparison between 3 machine learning algorithms: the xGboost model, the Random Forest algorithm and the K Nearest Neighbor algorithm. Each of them gave an accuracy respectively of 97.92 - 95 - 93.75. In the process of mapping flood-prone areas, the first model was relied upon, which gave the greatest accuracy (xGboost).

articleTitle: Spatiotemporal Analysis of LULC Impact on Surface Erosive Runoff (SER) Based SCS-CN Method
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Earth Observation and Geo-Spatial Information (ICEOGI)
abstract: This study aims to investigate the impact of the land use/land cover change on the calculation of the surface erosive runoff (SER) according the (SCS-CN) method. The results show that the SER production for the open forest, dense forest, and vegetation area classes decreased between 2010 and 2020, with the dominant SER production falling in the lower and medium classes (100–300 J mm h-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup>m-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>year:<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>). Agricultural practices such as crop rotation and ploughing appear to have exacerbated the erosive impact of stormy precipitation. The very high SER production class (>400 J mm h-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</sup> m-<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> year<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">-1</sup>) appears to remain stable, rarely exceeding 12 km<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>, The SER production for the urbanism class is generally low, usually staying below 10 km<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. Overall, the spatial variability of the SER has been greatly impacted by the land use and land cover (LULC) classes present in the region.

articleTitle: Deep Neural Networks for Water Quality Mapping
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Earth Observation and Geo-Spatial Information (ICEOGI)
abstract: Water is essential to the ecosystem, it has a significant role. Many factors influence water quality, including industrialization, pollution, and climate change. In this study, three coastal water quality parameters were mapped using Deep Neural Networks (DNN) combining in-situ measurements and Landsat-8 data. Indeed, three parameters measurements of Chlorophyll-a (Chl-a), Suspended Solids (SS), and Turbidity concentration and their relevant multispectral Landsat reflectances were used to train Back Propagation (BP) DNN. This paper focuses on the choice of the best model architecture which gives the optimum number of hidden layers and nods number's achieving the minimum of Root Mean Square Error (RMSE). When applying to Algerian coasts, the DNN result showed a correlation coefficient (R) of 97.19<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> with a 97.39 % of accuracy.

articleTitle: Impact of Transmitter Local Oscillator Spurious on SAR Images
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Earth Observation and Geo-Spatial Information (ICEOGI)
abstract: This paper studies the influence of local oscillator transmitter's spurious on SAR images. Synthetic spurious sam-ples have been generated and applied on the transmitting local oscillator signals. Series of measurements have been carried out and Back-Projection algorithm is applied on received data in order to obtain the SAR images. A degradation of the azimuth resolution is observed for <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-10 \ \mathbf{dBc}$</tex> spurious level at frequency shifts of 0.1 <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\mathbf{kHz}, 1 \ \mathbf{kHz}$</tex>. In addition, side-lobes levels which are close to the main lobe are increased by <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$1.2 \ \text{dB}$</tex>. However, spurious levels of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-30 \ \mathbf{dBc}$</tex> and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$-50 \ \mathbf{dBc}$</tex> do not have any impact on either azimuth resolution, side-lobes and speckle levels. Ground resolution is not affected by spurious signals.

articleTitle: Securing IoT Smart Irrigation Systems with Adapted Blockchain Based Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Earth Observation and Geo-Spatial Information (ICEOGI)
abstract: Blockchain (BC) technology promotes the scalability and stability of Internet of Things (IoT) applications and avoids the need for a single trusted authority. However, an IoT Smart Irrigation System (ISIS) comprises constrained devices such as microcontrollers and IoT gateways. A lightweight consensus mechanism is required to reduce computational costs in such systems. This paper presents a novel secure architecture for ISIS based on an adapted BC approach by implementing a lightweight Proof of Authority (PoA) consensus mechanism called Aura (Authority Round). The proposed mechanism is designed to overcome reported security limitations in commonly private BC. We apply our solution to the existing ISIS prototype developed in our laboratory. Experimental results show the feasibility and efficiency of BC technology in ISIS.

articleTitle: Along-Track Displacement Retrieval Using Sentinel-1 Images
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Earth Observation and Geo-Spatial Information (ICEOGI)
abstract: Both classic and Differential Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR & DInSAR) are used to detect and measure surface topography and deformations, in sensor's line of sight (LOS) direction. However, diverse phenomena such as earthquakes, volcanic eruptions, land subsidence, etc., can result in deformations in different directions including the sensor's movement direction (azimuth). This type of deformation can be detected using the phase of the backscattered signal and the Doppler spectra of the interferometric pairs. In this work, we focus on the application of Multiple Aperture Interferometry (MAI) for detecting surface and ground deformations in the azimuth direction. The effectiveness of this technique is demonstrated using a Sentinel-1 SLC image pair that covers the Thessaly region in Greece, hit by several earthquakes on March 2021, the largest of which was of 6.3 Magnitude. The results show that MAI can provide complementary information on deformations occurring in the azimuth direction, complementing the capabilities of DInSAR.

articleTitle: Urban Characterization Based On Recent Incoherent Polarimetric Decompositions
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Earth Observation and Geo-Spatial Information (ICEOGI)
abstract: This paper intends to characterize the urban area from PolSAR data using the incoherent Polarimetric Decomposition (PD) methods. These methods contribute intensively in interpreting the physical mechanisms of different land use and land covers. In this work, a comparison study is conducted using the existing PD methods in order to find which one has the capability to characterize better urban areas most accurately, regardless of how they are oriented relative to the radar line of sight (LOS). For this purpose, this study employed the three-component decomposition approach (FDD), the four component decomposition (Y4O), both without and with rotation of the coherency matrix, the six component decomposition (6SD), and the seven component decomposition (7SD). In order to assess the results, a PolSAR image acquired in L-band by RADARSAT-2 satellite over the San Francisco has been used.

articleTitle: Application of Modern GIS in Smart Grid
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Earth Observation and Geo-Spatial Information (ICEOGI)
abstract: The international's goal is to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 2050 through renewable energy sources by increasing solar and wind turbine farms. Simultaneously, the number of private micro-projects for residential rooftop solar panels is significantly increasing. As a result, the culture of consumers using electricity has changed, influencing the demand for electricity provided by the main supplier. However, there is a big concern about the stability of electricity production using renewable resources. Therefore, new management for the network is required for monitoring the demand and supplying the required electricity constantly. The smart grid is an application and technique that can help authorities and consumers achieve their goals and provide better services. This paper will discuss the application of modern GIS that will assist the modern management systems for implementing smart grids successfully as well as provide important information for consumers for optimal use of their microgrids. Two examples of asset inspection and demand monitoring will be given, and their result will be discussed here. Web GIS and online GIS methods were used for asset inspection. The focus on asset inspection was based on the effectiveness of web GIS and online GIS in monitoring and coordinating the assets without time restriction. The second example focused on the variation of the demand and how modern GIS can help the authorities to manage the grid.

articleTitle: AL-SBAS and EGNOS/GPS Performance for Cartographic Application in Africa
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Earth Observation and Geo-Spatial Information (ICEOGI)
abstract: Satellite Based Augmentation System (SBAS) provides an augmentation signal to Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS), in order to obtain better accuracy compared to GPS. This study is a contribution to using of the free SBAS service in the extended areas; this service is intended to offer a differential correction to users for general-purpose applications such as cartographic applications using satellite imagery. The use of satellite imagery with a high resolution (2.5 m), as Alsat-2A and Alsat-2B, the Algerian remote sensing satellites; necessitates a meter accuracy of at least 12 control points by scene and permit several applications as the middle scale cartography (1/50.000), rural cadastral map, forestry, etc., particularly when considering desertic areas in the Sahara. The performance of European Geostationary Navigation Overlay System (EGNOS) in considering the future setting-up of two RIMS stations in Algeria is evaluated in terms of availability and ionospheric error, in first time. The second objective of this paper is to analyse and study the reception degree of EGNOS signal in North Africa and at the edge coverage of EGNOS service without RIMS station (Ranging and Integrity Monitoring Stations) in Algeria. To realize this study, two Algerian sites (Oran, and particularly the Adrar site, more than 1000 km south) and two IGS sites (Rabat in Morocco, CPVG, city of Palmeira in Cape Verde) were used.

articleTitle: 3D Modeling of the Scientific and Educational Campus Borongaj Using Unmanned Aerial Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Earth Observation and Geo-Spatial Information (ICEOGI)
abstract: Significant urban development is ensured by the smart cities idea. In smaller regions, such as university campuses, an innovative approach towards using modern technologies for the purpose of strengthening infrastructures, exploitation of natural energy resources, and improving the quality of life can be employed. This paper focuses on the concept of a smart university campus and how drone technology can be used for its planning. The complete process of aerial photography is displayed, along with the preparations and post-processing steps required. It is described how to create a three-dimensional model of the observed campus and how to conduct potential analyses using the model that was created.

articleTitle: PolSAR Data Classification Using Extreme Gradient Boosting Classifier
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Earth Observation and Geo-Spatial Information (ICEOGI)
abstract: This work explored the extreme gradient boosting classifier (XGBoost) to classify land cover using PolSAR (Polarimetric Synthetic aperture radar) data. The XGBoost is a type of Ensemble learning algorithms. These algorithms have attracted many researchers in the classification of remote sensing data since they outperform other Machine Learning ML methods in terms of accuracy. In this work, the compensated Kenaugh matrix's diagonal elements and the Six Components Decomposition Method (6SDM) components were combined and used as a feature vector to feed the classifier. ALOS-2 L band data over the San Francisco, USA was used to test the used classifier's performance. The results show that XGBoost outperformed SVM, KNN, and RF classifiers in terms of accuracy.

articleTitle: Motion Of Rainy Cells Observed In Radar Images
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Earth Observation and Geo-Spatial Information (ICEOGI)
abstract: The determination of the intensity and direction of rainy cloud motion is one of the problems raised when issuing weather forecasting. In this study, we examine the optical flow equation-based identification and extraction of rainy cell velocity fields from radar images. The motion of precipitation was analyzed with two different methods of optical flow: the local estimate employing a fractional variation model and the global motion model of Horn and Schunck. Both methods describe very well the trajectory and evolution of velocity fields in the radar images. Applying the differential method of 'Horn & Schunck on a rainy cell isolated from radar images, allowed us to detect the direction and the motion of the precipitation The fractional variation produces better results than the Horn & Schunck technique because it is more precise and produces a dense velocity field, although taking more time to analyze

articleTitle: Change Detection in Multitemporal SAR Images: A Multiresolution Analysis and Hypothesis Testing Approach
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Earth Observation and Geo-Spatial Information (ICEOGI)
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) is an effective tool for detecting environmental changes over time. Its ability to provide images of high-resolution in any kind of weather conditions and its independence of daylight make it a valuable asset in monitoring and management of environmental changes. This paper presents a new method for detecting changes in multitemporal SAR images without the use of speckle filtering. The approach consists of: (1) creating a multiresolution set from the ratio image through the ratio of each scale of the two intensity SAR images after being processed with the stationary wavelet transform (SWT); (2) conducting hypothesis testing on the multiresolution ratio image set; and (3) combining the results at the optimal reliable scale to produce the resultant map of change. The effectiveness of this method was demonstrated through experiments on semi-simulated RADARSAT-2 satellite SAR images in Algiers region.

articleTitle: Towards a SOLAP Based Decision Support System for Forest Fire Management
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Earth Observation and Geo-Spatial Information (ICEOGI)
abstract: Risk, suppression, and damage assessment are essential parts of forest fire management. The involved data is distributed and heterogeneous, concerning meteorology, topomorphology, and socio-economy. In addition, it has a multiscale spatiotemporal analysis aspect. These reinforce the need to use the appropriate methods and technologies to enhance decision-making. This research investigates the potential of adopting spatial data warehousing techniques to build a SOLAP-based DSS that supports the whole decisional chain. (i) source collection and integration; (ii) data repository design and population; (iii) SOLAP analytics; and finally, (iv) data visualization in numerous formats, including tabular, graphic, and dynamic maps.

articleTitle: Availability and Accessibility of Open Data Relevant for Urban Planning: A Case Study of Zagreb, Croatia
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Earth Observation and Geo-Spatial Information (ICEOGI)
abstract: Sustainable urban development (planning) relies on up-to-date spatial and other information. Much of this data comes from government organizations, agencies and institutions which are obliged to make it open by the EU Open Data Directive (2019/1024) and Implementing Regulation (2023/138). The City of Zagreb has established spatial data infrastructure (SDI) to support the provision of spatial open government data. This paper analyses which government data relevant to urban planning is available in Zagreb SDI, in which form it can be assessed and to what extent is this data in line with the list of adopted high-value data in Europe. The results indicate that a number of spatial data exist, but data accessibility limits its reuse potential - data mostly available as view only.

articleTitle: Neighborhood Selection and Cholesky Matrix for CAPON-based SAR Tomography Inversion
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Earth Observation and Geo-Spatial Information (ICEOGI)
abstract: Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) Tomography gain particular interest due to its 3-D reconstruction capability in built-up areas. Spectral estimation approach enables the scene reflectivity to be restored from multi-baseline SAR datasets. The lack of a priori information about the observed regions and the need for high-accuracy reconstructions encourage researchers to use non-parametric multi-looking spectral estimation methods. These estimators require the generation of the Multidimensional Covariance Matrix (MCM) by means of a local spatial averaging operation. In this context, the paper's aim is to contribute to the tomographic process development by: 1) considering an appropriate selection of surrounding neighbors for the data covariance matrix estimation, where the boxcar window is replaced by a range-oriented rectangular window; and 2) incorporating the root square matrix of the MCM (also known as the Cholesky matrix) into the CAPON-based spectral analysis algorithm. The experimental results on data acquired by TerraSAR-X satellite demonstrate the effectiveness of the proposed tomographic neighborhood selection, along with the potential of the improved CAPON-based estimator in regard to scatterers' height estimation.

articleTitle: Detecting and Counting Area of Crop Fields in Sentinel-2 Images Using Mask R-CNN Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Earth Observation and Geo-Spatial Information (ICEOGI)
abstract: Agriculture is a vital activity in many countries around the world, and statistics play an important role in understanding its current state. By gathering data on production levels, land use, crop yields and other factors related to agriculture, governments can make informed decisions about how best to support this sector of their economy. In addition to being used by government officials for policy making purposes, agricultural statistics are also valuable resources for researchers studying the impact of climate change or food security issues. For this reason, the direction of agriculture of Djelfa made every season statistic of all the activities in the region. This work was made by the engineers and the agents of the direction by visiting the farm and investigate farmers. This task is difficult and will be more difficult according to the increase of the agriculture lands. The using of the technology may facilitate this task. The aim of this work is to use the novel technology like satellite images and artificial intelligence to compute areas of important crops on the region like cereal, forage. We try to apply on Sentinel-2 images a recent model of deep learning the mask R-CNN algorithm that allow to detect and mask objects which are in our case the crop fields.

articleTitle: Geographic Information System for Air Traffic Optimization Based on Simulated Annealing in Training Environment
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Earth Observation and Geo-Spatial Information (ICEOGI)
abstract: To ensure the safety and fluidity of air traffic, the air traffic controller applies a set of rules dictated by the ICAO, called separation rules. For this, the controller must first undergo training based in part on practical work in simulated traffic management. From a traffic configuration given by flight plans (FPL) of an exercise, the trainee controller can detect any conflicts that may arise between each pair of aircraft and act accordingly by changing part of the FPL of the one of the planes (or both) so as to avoid a risk of collision. At the end of the exercise, a debriefing is organized to discuss the effectiveness of the trainee's decisions and compare them with the solutions proposed by his instructor. We propose in this work, to reinforce this training by proposing to the trainee a tool which can generate an additional solution (in addition to that of the instructor). For this, we use a GIS for geographic data and a metaheuristic, simulated annealing, for traffic optimization. The objectives to be achieved are: the elimination of conflicts between aircraft, the minimization of the distance traveled by the aircraft and the minimization of the changes made in relation to the initial flight plan. The evaluation of this work goes through several tests carried out on part of the Algerian airspace with the same practical exercises used in training.

articleTitle: Modernization of Geoinformatics Curriculum Based on Problem-Based Learning - Experiences of the GEOBIZ Project
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Earth Observation and Geo-Spatial Information (ICEOGI)
abstract: Geospatial data, one of the key forces behind the current digital revolution, is the foundation of the geoinformatics ecosystem. Because geoinformatics is used in many different fields, it is crucial that geoinformatics experts have a quality education. The core of geoinformatics is new, cutting-edge technology that is used to support the development of applications for specific purposes, and one of the challenges that the geoinformatics ecosystem currently faces is the academic sector's tardiness in integrating new technologies into the teaching process. As a result, new specialists got the information and abilities needed by the labor market. Several initiatives are working to find solutions to this issue on a worldwide scope, which will encourage the modernization of the geoinformatics curriculum. The Erasmus+ program through Sector Skills Alliances (SSA) and Capacity Building in Higher Education (CBHE) provides academic institutions a tool for implementing curriculum modernization projects and finding new approaches in academic education. At the CBHE call in 2019, funding was approved for the project “Business driven problem-based learning for academic excellence in geoinformatics” (GEOBIZ), which is led by the Faculty of Geodesy of the University of Zagreb. The goal of GEOBIZ project is to improve the geoinformatics ecosystem through the development of a new and innovative model of cooperation between the business and academic sectors that will support the academic sector in modernizing study programs through problem-based learning following the technological and conceptual changes in geoinformatics. This project will update some geoinformatics research in order to raise future specialists' profiles and better match them to the demands of the market. Another objective is to create a cooperation model that would help all stakeholders in the geoinformatics ecosystem. This paper presents the GEOBIZ methodology and findings.

articleTitle: Bagging Ensemble Based on Multi-Layer Perceptron Neural Network for Landslide Susceptibility Assessment
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Earth Observation and Geo-Spatial Information (ICEOGI)
abstract: Landslide susceptibility assessment is the most appropriate method to mitigate the landslide threat for both populations and infrastructure. The development of accurate and reliable susceptibility models is therefore essential for sustainable development in landslide-prone regions. The present study proposes an implementation of the Bagging (BG) ensemble using the Multi-layer Perceptron Neural Network (MLP). The aim of this work is to reduce the variance of the MLP using the bootstrapping method of the BG ensemble. To estimate the potential of the ensemble, a fine-tuned individual MLP was implemented for benchmarking. A spatial database with 115 landslides and 12 causal factors was collected to implement the modelling. For separating training and test data, repeated K-fold cross-validation was used. The prediction capability of the models was estimated using the area under (AUC) the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve (AUC), the root mean square error (RMSE), the F1 and the accuracy scores. The results indicated that the BG ensemble outperformed the individual MLP in all the assessment measures. The BG-MLP model is more robust and generalizable, resulting in higher scores with a reduced standard deviation compared to the individual MLP. Therefore, the BG-MLP ensemble was successfully produced for the assessment of landslide susceptibility and demonstrated significantly improved results.

articleTitle: Forest Tree Species Classification Using Machine Learning and Satellite Images
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Earth Observation and Geo-Spatial Information (ICEOGI)
abstract: Forests play a vital role in our ability to thrive, and their significance in our lives cannot be overstated. In forestry, machine learning has found diverse applications, with tree species classification being one of the most significant. This task involves categorising trees into groups, such as genera or families, and can greatly benefit from the utilisation of Remote Sensing (RS) images, which allow for remote assessment of forest conditions and facilitate effective forest management. The objective of this paper was to classify forest tree species using remote sensing images acquired from the Sentinel-2 satellite and Vegetation Indices (VIs). Three VIs were calculated: the Normalised Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), the Enhanced Vegetation Index (EVI), and the Atmospherically Resistant Vegetation Index (ARVI). Subsequently, three major machine learning classification algorithms, namely Decision Tree, Random Forest, and Support Vector Machine, were selected for the classification task. The performance of these algorithms was compared using four evaluation metrics: precision, recall, F-score, and accuracy. The results revealed that Random Forest outperformed the other algorithms, achieving an accuracy of 0.76, precision of 0.71, recall of 0.72, and F-score of 0.71. This research contributes to the advancement of tree species classification using remote sensing images and machine learning techniques, with potential applications in forest management and conservation.

articleTitle: Seismic Hazard Mapping in Northwestern Algeria
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Earth Observation and Geo-Spatial Information (ICEOGI)
abstract: Northern Algeria is a part of the Eurasia-Africa tectonic plates boundary, consequently, it is a prone area for occurrence of earthquakes. We propose in this work to assess and map peak ground acceleration in northwestern Algeria by using the PSHA method. The methodology includes the following four steps: (i) Identification of seismic sources, (ii) Determination of sources parameters, (iii) Definition of ground motion attenuation model and finally, (iv) Assessment and mapping of seismic hazard. The obtained results are shown in terms of curves of annual frequencies of exceedance versus acceleration (PGA), as strong motion scenario for the Oran city by performing a deaggregation analysis and a uniform hazard spectrum (UHS), as well as 475 years return period acceleration map.

articleTitle: Pansharpening Methods Based on a Redundant Contourlet Transform
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Earth Observation and Geo-Spatial Information (ICEOGI)
abstract: The pansharpening of high-resolution panchromatic (Pan) image and low-resolution multispectral (MS) images represents an important task in the remote sensing field. It allows the joint exploitation of the information derived from both types of images. However, this may cause a distortion of spectral information or a lack in details and structures. The multiresolution analysis using wavelet transforms has proved its efficiency in the pansharpening domain, due to the representation of the image content over different resolution levels. In image fusion applications, we always need more detail information to be incorporated in the pansharpening procedure in order to produce enhanced results. However, the limitation of the wavelet transform to three types of oriented detail coefficients prevents this need from being met. To overcome this limitation, we propose to use the redundant contourlet transform (RCT) which extracts a richer multiscale directional information from the image. For this purpose, two RCT-based pansharpening methods are introduced and suitable data fusion procedures are described. We conducted several experiments on two different datasets acquired respectively by ALSAT-2A and IKONOS satellites. The visual results as well as quantitative results from evaluation metrics demonstrate the performance of the proposed methods.

articleTitle: Morphodynamics of a Breakwater-Protected Sandspit: 16 Years of Digital Elevation Models
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Earth Observation and Geo-Spatial Information (ICEOGI)
abstract: Sand spits are common dynamic features in river inlets that may protect river margins and communities from ocean storm wave and impacts. The morphodynamics of the estuarine spit of the Douro river was studied to assess the spits reaction to the extension and construction of breakwaters, aimed at spit stabilization. Since the intervention, the spit has almost doubled in volume, growing predominantly towards the new detached breakwater in the west. However, this growth has decelerated in recent years, suggesting that the spit is reaching a stable state.

articleTitle: Clustering Enhancement Using Particle Swarm Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Earth Observation and Geo-Spatial Information (ICEOGI)
abstract: Clustering aims to find useful groups of objects (clusters), based on the closest distance to clusters centers. Soft Subspace Clustering algorithms are generally formulated as an optimization problem that minimizes an objective function, which makes a great improvement in classification. However, each time several iterations to determine the best cluster center are required. In addition, objective function optimization does not always find the global minimum but some local ones. In this paper, We have introduced the algorithm of Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), which is combined with two subspace clustering algorithms to enhance the clusters centers positions. the proposed classification method has been tested on a synthetic and aerial data set. Two metrics have been used to compare and validate the final results: Normalized Mutual Information (NMI) and classification accuracy. The clustering results obtained are good and improved.

articleTitle: Simulated Data for SAR Tomographic Reconstruction in Urban Areas
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Earth Observation and Geo-Spatial Information (ICEOGI)
abstract: The evaluation of SAR tomographic reconstruction models requires an examination of their robustness with respect to various parameters. Typically, a simple simulation of reflectivity profiles with different scatters at different elevations and SNRs is used to evaluate the robustness of any reconstruction model. However, these simulation setups do not account for most of the geometric acquisition variables present in the reconstruction of real data. Most of the data used for SAR tomographic reconstruction in urban areas are acquired using high-resolution X-band sensors because of their weak penetration, which aids in recovering the geometry of the target. In this work, we propose simulating an urban area acquisition scene that considers the primary acquisition parameters of high-resolution X-band sensors. By doing so, one can simulate various measurements for different building shapes and elevations, providing a more comprehensive evaluation of the reconstruction methods. In this simulation, the geometry of SAR tomography is respected by considering different geometry distortions such as layover, foreshortening, and shadowing. The simulation is evaluated by implementing different reconstruction methods to the simulated data. Results obtained show that sparse reconstruction methods such as 11 and 12 norms and SL1MMER are more suitable to evaluate the reconstruction due to the high-resolution acquisitions. On the other hand, we used other conventional reconstruction models such as SVD-Weiner and MUSIC for assessment purposes.

articleTitle: Application of Digital Twin in City Management
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Earth Observation and Geo-Spatial Information (ICEOGI)
abstract: The trend of rapid urbanization brings numerous challenges for urban environments, whereby the concept of smart cities is imposed as a solution to the current and future challenges of managing cities and improving the quality of life of citizens. The development of the concept of smart cities is stimulated by the development of innovative technologies, and their application improves city processes, services, sustainability, and the economy. The successful implementation of new city management concepts is made possible by the creation of virtual copies of urban environments, materialized in the context of digital twins. Digital twins are being created today in all aspects of human activity such as manufacturing, space industry, medicine, and many others. In the context of urban management, digital twins are established in different levels: for a part of a city, a smart district or at the level of an entire city. As part of this paper, a 3D model was developed for the test area of the city of Pula in Croatia, which is the backbone for the establishment of the digital twin of the city. The main purpose of establishing such virtual platform is to point out the possibilities of application through analysis, simulation, optimization, and predicting.

articleTitle: Multicriteria Ensemble Learning for Multispectral Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Earth Observation and Geo-Spatial Information (ICEOGI)
abstract: In this paper, we propose a multicriteria aggregation approach for an ensemble of well-known classifiers using the Analytical Hierarchy Process (AHP) for the purpose of deriving a globally efficient land cover classifier. The land is the basis for most biological and human activities on the earth. Specifically, agriculture, forestry, industries, transport, housing, and other services all use the land as a natural and/or economic resource. Land cover and land use data classification are essential for observing and managing a range of key environmental and socioeconomic trends, many of which are linked to the sustainable use of resources and climate change. In the last decades, numerous classification algorithms have been proposed to tackle this problem. However, as there is no universal classifier for all types of data distributions, thus, each classifier, which relies its operation on a different principle, may attain a different degree of accuracy in a specific application problem. As a simple and effective methodology, an ensemble of classifiers has been applied to several classification problems aiming to improve performance and increase reliability. We apply our approach to land cover mapping on Sentinel-2 Satellite images and preliminary results are promising.

articleTitle: Remote Sensing-Based Model for Estimating Groundwater Pumping: Case Study of Irrigated Perimeter of the Medjerda Lower Valley, Tunisia
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Earth Observation and Geo-Spatial Information (ICEOGI)
abstract: The estimation of groundwater exploitation in arid and semi-arid countries such as Tunisia remains a challenging issue. In the Medjerda lower basin, water resources are overexploited due to Climate Change, anthropogenic pressures, and the intensification of irrigated areas. To address this, estimating spatially distributed crop water consumption is crucial for promoting efficient water management. This study aims to estimate volumes of groundwater pumping for irrigation in a citrus orchard area of the Medjerda Lower Valley basin using earth observation data as input of the SAtellite Monitoring of Irrigation (SAMIR) model based on the FAO-56 dual crop coefficient water balance model. The SAMIR model's simulated irrigation volumes were compared with the actual volumes of water that were supplied by farmers. The results showed significant difference between the simulated required volumes of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{1252074 \ \mathrm{m}^{3}}$</tex> and the declared amount of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$663 \ 882 \ \mathrm{m}^{3}$</tex>, indicating an estimated groundwater irrigation pumping of about <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$239 \ 813 \ \mathrm{m}^{3}/\text{year}$</tex>. These findings confirm the feasibility of earth observation data for estimating irrigation groundwater pumping in water-scarce areas, and that they can be useful for decision-makers.

articleTitle: Contribution of Remote Sensing and GIS in the Analysis of Landscape Ecology: Case of the High Steppe Plains of Algeria
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Earth Observation and Geo-Spatial Information (ICEOGI)
abstract: Remote sensing integrated with geographic information systems (GIS) has opened new perspectives in environmental studies. In the field of sustainable management of steppe rangelands, it allows in particular to draw up the land cover map (LCM) which is needed to evaluate the sensitivity of the rangelands to disturbances (desertification, water erosion, soil salination …). This study presents a quantitative analysis of a landscape for a sustainable management of rangelands and the proposed methods for ecosystem restoration. The method is illustrated on a sub-watershed of the region of Messad-Ain El Ibel, with priority of intervention to water erosion. The steps followed are: (1) elaboration of the LCM by supervised classification. The kappa coefficient (83.9<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup>) indicates that the classification is sufficiently correct; (2) extraction of an area with urgent intervention priority against water erosion; (3) generalization of the Land Cover Map, and its smoothing by filters (Majority and Boundary clean tool); (4) finally, a quantitative analysis of the landscape using Fragstats. 10,040 patches were found. After generalizing by filter functions, the patches number per class decreased for all classes, a fragmentation indicate show that are moderately to weakly fragmented and The Shannon and the Simpson Diversity Index indicate that this diversity is maintained.

articleTitle: Internet-of-Things and Wireless Sensor Networks as Enablers for Soil Observation in Smallholder Farms
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Earth Observation and Geo-Spatial Information (ICEOGI)
abstract: Smallholder farms are known to be resource-constrained and remotely located, which makes in-situ data collection challenging. Typically, on-farm data deficiency arises and little support for farming decisions is one cause of poor production. Automated, precise, and affordable data collection and dissemination methods are vital to fill this data gap. The Internet of Things (IoT) and wireless sensor networks (WSNs) are tools fitting the bill, but they require careful design and deployment for local contexts. Our work is an attempt to define an IoT-Wsnsystem as a digital data infrastructure for in-season farm monitoring in rural smallholder farms. Design considerations are identified to enhance system reliability and robustness. A wireless communication protocol that runs reliably in a resource-constrained environment is identified, devices with ease of access, configuration, and maintenance were selected, and an appropriate sampling strategy to address a wide area with minimum resource consumption is designed. LoRa nodes with soil physical property sensors have been distributed among representative farm plots for data collection. And data was sent, autonomously to a back-end system over cellular communication. Our experience reveals the potential of the technology to generate as much required data as needed but with further careful design issues.

articleTitle: GIS and IoT Integration: A State of the Art and Challenges
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Earth Observation and Geo-Spatial Information (ICEOGI)
abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) is one of the most important technologies of the century. This ubiquitous paradigm generates valuable data in which the geospatial aspect is crucial to unlock its full potential. Every Geographic Information System (GIS) provides three main functionalities: data acquisition, data analysis and data mapping, that lack the ability to deal with real-time heterogeneous data and must be adjusted to fit the new needs and challenges. Indeed, many research works make use of GIS in IoT environments. Nevertheless, it is not obvious to make an efficient deployment of these systems with the current challenges, which gives good opportunities to explore the integration of GIS and IoT that is promising. In this paper, we present A state of the art of this topic and discuss some issues that must be considered. We focus more on geographical data acquisition since it is the first layer in GIS-IoT architecture and any error in this phase may be irreversible. Therefore, we propose to decompose it into three sub-functionalities: data collection, data transmission, and data storage.

articleTitle: Data Cubes – A Modern Approach for Handling Earth Observation Data

articleTitle: Monitoring Lake Chad Basin Water Quality Using Earth Observation Satellite Observations
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Earth Observation and Geo-Spatial Information (ICEOGI)
abstract: The surface waters of the Lake Chad Basin are under threat from climate change and anthropogenic influence. Access to reliable information on the status and evolution of water resources and of their multiple uses is a major challenge for sustainable water resource management. Indeed, water quality monitoring has become one of the most important element of environmental management of the basin's aquatic ecosystems and is essential to provide information and rapid response on its impacts on human health, food production, ecosystem functioning, biodiversity and economic growth. This monitoring has been made possible by the Copernicus program, which has opened up new avenues for satellite applications and services through its free, full and open access basis to high-resolution sensors such as those on-board the two Sentinel-2 (A and B) optical satellites. Thus, the use of remote sensing data from these two satellites allows for addressing and informing communities and stakeholders about water quality changes. A joint effort by CBLT and UNESCO with the support of a French consortium (CNES, INRAE, IRD, OFB, and Magellium as a contractor) has made possible to process a large dataset of Sentinel-2 images over the Lake Chad Basin. The satellite data revealed that the region experiences high variability in water quality as a function of climatic conditions that control the water body's surface area, water turbidity, and productivity. Indeed, a change in turbidity affects the amount of light that can penetrate through the water column, with consequences for photosynthetic processes. Eutrophication in Lake Chad, monitored by the Chlorophyll-a pigment associated with phytoplankton, showed seasonal variability with low eutrophication (Chlorophyll-a content of about 10 ug/L) during the winter and high eutrophication at the end of the dry season (June) with Chlorophyll-a content up to 85 µg/L locally.

articleTitle: Evaluation Techniques for PolSAR Speckle Filtering
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Earth Observation and Geo-Spatial Information (ICEOGI)
abstract: Speckle noise is the biggest drawback that affects polarimetric SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar) images. Due to its multiplicative nature, it degrades their quality, complicates their interpretation and reduces the information accuracy. Its effect is reduced by applying polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) filtering methods. In the literature, there are several methods of PolSAR filtering, it is not obvious to choose the most effective filter, and among the techniques for evaluating the performance of these filters, it is difficult to find the best analysis method that leads to the best filtering quality without information loss. In this paper, we present a comparative study of evaluation methods for polarimetric SAR filters considering three criteria: smoothing of homogeneous areas, edge preservation and conservation of polarimetric information. In this work, we propose a more simplified approach to evaluate a polarimetric SAR filter. Each criterion includes study techniques that will help to identify the analysis method that will facilitate the selection of the best filter.

articleTitle: Land Use and Land Cover Change Detection Based on Urban Spectral Indices: A Case Study of the Coastal Municipalities of Annaba Province, Algeria
publicationTitle: 2023 International Conference on Earth Observation and Geo-Spatial Information (ICEOGI)
abstract: Deriving accurate and timely data on land use and land cover change (LULCC) from satellite imagery is essential for sustainable coastal management. This research's objective is to assess, evaluate, and monitor the nature and extent of LULCC in the coastal municipalities of Annaba Province in Algeria using Landsat 7 and Landsat 8 images through the period from 2000 to 2015 and Sentinel-2A images between 2015 and 2019. The image differencing change detection technique was applied based on five urban spectral indices. Urban indices maximize sensitivity to the spectral characteristics of artificial (built-up areas, paved surfaces, mines, etc.) and bare land due to their spectral similarity compared to other LULC types. In the difference (change) images of the derived indices, the positive change pixel values essentially characterize an increase in artificial and bare land, except for one differenced index-the negative change values mainly indicate the same increase. The footprint of this increase was extracted using the random forest classifier, and the classification accuracy was assessed using a stratified random sampling design. The findings showed that the computed accuracy measures varied according to the used image data and spectral index from one municipality to another. For Annaba municipality, the obtained user's accuracy values range from 90.48 to 94.44% for Landsat data and between 70.59 and 80% concerning Sentinel-2A data. To enhance the estimated area proportions of the increase in artificial and bare land, certain changes in surface conditions, such as those in agricultural fields due to pre- and post-harvest conditions, were excluded using Geographic Information System (GIS) techniques. According to the accuracy assessment results, the image differencing approach based on the selected urban indices provided accurate detection of LULCC.

Author Keywords: land use and land cover change
